findings.claim: On April 7, 2026, Tuttle Capital Management changed the ticker of The SPAC and New Issue ETF from SPCX to SPCK, stating that the change would not affect that fund's objective, strategy, or fees.
findings.source_title: Tuttle Capital's SPAC and New Issue ETF to Change Ticker to SPCK

findings.claim: Space Exploration Technologies Corp., a Texas corporation, priced its IPO of Class A common stock at $135.00 per share and was approved to list on Nasdaq and Nasdaq Texas under the symbol SPCX; the June 11, 2026 prospectus said that if the underwriters' option was exercised in full Elon Musk would hold about 82.3% of voting power and the company would be a Nasdaq controlled company because Class B shares carry 10 votes.
findings.source_title: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Rule 424(b)(4) prospectus

findings.claim: In June 2026 SpaceX completed the IPO by selling 638.9 million Class A shares at $135.00, including the full underwriters' option, for net proceeds of $85,675 million after $575 million of underwriting commissions and offering costs.
findings.source_title: SpaceX Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, SpaceX reported revenue of $14,575 million, up from $5,576 million a year earlier, income from operations of $2,791 million versus a loss of $273 million, and net income of $4,404 million versus a net loss of $1,054 million.
findings.source_title: SpaceX Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, SpaceX still reported a net loss of $413 million and an accumulated deficit of $37,448 million, and the quarter's net income included a $561 million unrealized gain on an equity-method investment in TBC, an entity the filing says is controlled by the CEO.
findings.source_title: SpaceX Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Third-quarter 2026 segment revenue was $7,560 million in Super Intelligence, $5,248 million in Connectivity, and $1,767 million in Space, while the Space segment lost $7 million from operations in the quarter and $1,211 million for the nine months, with Space research and development of $1,225 million in the quarter.
findings.source_title: SpaceX Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Starlink consumer subscribers were 13.6 million at September 30, 2026, up from 7.2 million a year earlier, while consumer ARPU was $69 in the third quarter versus $83 in the year-ago quarter.
findings.source_title: SpaceX Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Connectivity enterprise and government revenue was $2,127 million in the third quarter of 2026, up from $1,111 million a year earlier, and Launch and Development revenue, which the filing describes as government-agency space programs, was $637 million in the quarter.
findings.source_title: SpaceX Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: In the third quarter of 2026, Customer B accounted for 34.5% of consolidated revenue, all in the SI segment, Customer A accounted for 16.6% across all three segments, and one customer accounted for 27.7% of accounts receivable.
findings.source_title: SpaceX Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Backlog was $62,959 million at September 30, 2026, of which $17,520 million was already recorded as deferred revenue, with about 67% expected to be recognized within one year and about 27% in one to three years.
findings.source_title: SpaceX Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: At September 30, 2026, debt principal was $38,006 million, including $25,000 million of senior unsecured notes issued in June 2026 at coupons of 5.350% to 6.650% with a 5.855% weighted-average coupon and first maturity on July 15, 2031, and related-party Valor equipment financing recorded as $2,181 million current and $10,716 million long-term debt.
findings.source_title: SpaceX Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Management said existing liquidity should cover cash needs for at least the next twelve months, citing $51,294 million of cash and cash equivalents, $38,561 million of short-term marketable securities, and $5,000 million undrawn on the SpaceX credit facility at September 30, 2026.
findings.source_title: SpaceX Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: Nameplate compute, defined as installed GPU power and not actual utilization, was 1.7 gigawatts at September 30, 2026, up from 0.6 gigawatts a year earlier.
findings.source_title: SpaceX Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: SpaceX flew 33 Falcon launches in the third quarter of 2026, down from 43 a year earlier, of which 12 were customer launches versus 15, and it flew 2 Starship launches, all of which the company still classifies as internal.
findings.source_title: SpaceX Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: On August 14, 2026 SpaceX closed the merger of Anysphere, Inc. (Cursor) for an implied equity value of $60 billion paid in Class A common stock, and weighted-average basic shares for the quarter were 11,942 million versus 2,941 million a year earlier after retroactive adjustment for the May 2026 five-for-one split.
findings.source_title: SpaceX Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

findings.claim: The 10-Q discloses multiple 2026 lawsuits alleging that Grok image tools enabled nonconsensual explicit images of women and children, a EUR 120 million European Commission Digital Services Act fine imposed on December 5, 2025 and appealed, a Vidstream jury award of $105 million plus $67 million of prejudgment interest that is on appeal, and a litigation accrual of $350 million at September 30, 2026.
findings.source_title: SpaceX Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026

upcoming_catalysts.event: Recognition of about 67% of the $62,959 million September 30, 2026 backlog within one year.
Possible release of a significant portion of the valuation allowance on U.S. deferred tax assets, which management says would produce a material tax benefit if positive evidence becomes available.

policy_links.policy: Government-agency space launch and spacecraft development programs
policy_links.bottleneck: orbital access and crewed or cargo spacecraft
policy_links.revenue_mechanism: Fixed-price Launch and Development contracts are recognized over time using a cost-to-cost method. The 10-Q reports $637 million of that revenue in the third quarter of 2026.

policy_links.policy: Digital Services Act enforcement against X, including the European Commission's December 5, 2025 decision and EUR 120 million fine, now before the EU General Court
policy_links.revenue_mechanism: The disclosed effect is a fine and compliance burden on the X business, not a contract or order that produces SpaceX revenue.

key_risks.risk: Customer B was 34.5% of third-quarter revenue and that revenue sits entirely in the SI segment, so one SI relationship can move consolidated results.

Elon Musk was expected to hold about 82.3% of the vote if the IPO option was fully exercised, Class B shares have 10 votes and elect a majority of the board, and the company said it would rely on Nasdaq controlled-company exemptions.
Grok image-generation litigation, the appealed EUR 120 million DSA fine, and other listed cases are open, with a $350 million accrual and other possible losses the company says it cannot estimate.

Debt principal was $38.0 billion, including a large related-party equipment facility with Valor, and interest expense was $1,968 million for the first nine months of 2026, of which $864 million was related-party.
The NAACP sued over mobile gas turbines at the COLOSSUS II data center, alleging Clean Air Act permit violations and seeking an injunction against turbine operation.

dilution_events_last_12m.description: February 2, 2026 common-control share exchange in which SpaceX acquired X.AI Holdings Corp. The 10-Q does not state a cash purchase price.

June 2026 IPO of 638.9 million Class A shares at $135.00, including the full greenshoe, for net proceeds of $85,675 million after $575 million of commissions and offering costs. Outstanding redeemable convertible preferred stock converted into Class A and Class B common stock in connection with the IPO.
August 14, 2026 acquisition of Anysphere, Inc. (Cursor) at an implied equity value of $60 billion, paid in Class A common stock plus cash for fractional shares.

notes: SPCX is Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Class A common stock. The previous SPCX, Tuttle Capital's SPAC and New Issue ETF, changed its ticker to SPCK effective April 7, 2026. The prospectus voting figure of about 82.3% assumes full exercise of the underwriters' option. The 10-Q confirms that exercise but does not restate Musk's voting power after the August 14, 2026 Cursor share issuance. As of October 15, 2026 the 10-Q reports 8,246,541,218 Class A shares and 5,334,522,491 Class B shares. The May 2026 five-for-one split is retroactively reflected in share counts and is not an economic dilution. All Starship launches to date are classified as internal, and the company recognizes no inter-segment revenue for Starlink launches. Management states liquidity is sufficient for at least twelve months. No going-concern paragraph and no disclosed material weakness were found in the Q3 10-Q. A separate earnings exhibit described a Starship flight as revenue-generating because it carried Starlink V3 satellites; that wording was not used here because the 10-Q classifies those launches as internal.
